name: Eric Jing Du
title: Steve and Wendy Blum Professor; UF Research Foundation Professor; ICIC Lab Director
department: Civil and Coastal Engineering; affiliate/graduate faculty in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering and Industrial and Systems Engineering
fitReason: Strong applied embodied-AI methods match spanning LLM sequence planning, tactile multimodal foundation models and force-guided imitation. Appropriate project scoping is important because some recent learning studies are dataset/simulation work while current physical teleoperation can be rule-based.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full 2023 RoboGPT preprint explicitly documents GPT-4-generated actions decoded and sent to a Franka Emika Panda, with real five-soft-block stacking in §IV-A/Figure7; the figure was visually checked. Primitive execution uses conventional control and simplified object labels. Its80 pipeline-planning trials are Unity simulation, not80 real-robot runs. Current 2026 TEGA verifies actual Panda/Allegro/DIGIT hardware, but §III-B explicitly uses rule-based EMG mapping and calibrated tactile features; it is not credited as a new neural-control deployment. Physical20 reflects older verified learned-planning execution, without assuming 2027 access.

shortVisit.summary: The current ICIC site and 2025 recruitment flyer advertise a Spring 2026 Civil Engineering PhD RA position for AI/autonomous drones. It is a degree-admission opportunity, not a short-term visiting-master’s invitation. No current external short-visit or summer 2027 offer was verified.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct LLM-guided robot assembly, multimodal tactile foundation models and robot imitation methods.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual GPT4-planned arm execution is 2023; current hardware corroborated but recent TEGA is rule-based.
